scenario.name: Microsoft MSTIC, Volexity & CISA ED 21-02 DFIR — Exchange HttpProxy, MSExchange Management & OAB Webshell Forensics
scenario.overview: Imagine a modern glass office building where visitors check in with the front-desk receptionist, scan a badge at the lobby turnstile, and walk between glass-walled meeting rooms. In the sunlit office building lobby, an unbadged visitor talks past the front-desk receptionist and persuades the desk clerk to print a temporary building pass. In this real-world scenario, the intruder smuggles copied records out past the lobby badge turnstile in tiny disguised batches, then smuggles copied records out past the lobby badge turnstile in tiny disguised batches. When building security compares the receptionist sign-in sheet against the turnstile badge swipes across the glass offices, the unescorted hallway trail is exposed. In this scenario (T1190, Microsoft MSTIC, Volexity & CISA ED 21-02 DFIR, Exchange HttpProxy, MSExchange Management & OAB Webshell Forensics), the attacker follows one continuous intrusion path so each later Step can show the exact handoff that makes the next stage possible. The attack unfolds in one continuous arc: exchange Frontend HttpProxy Log Analysis, then exchange Management Log, then aSP.NET Dynamic Compilation. Steps #1–#3 walk that chain end-to-end by covering Exchange Frontend HttpProxy Log Analysis, then Exchange Management Log, then ASP.NET Dynamic Compilation, while the Process Hierarchy tab keeps the Parent → Child spawn tree visible so you can see which trusted process launched the next payload. Primary detection correlates Sysmon Event 1 with the documented host and network chain.

stages.title: Stage 1: Exchange Frontend HttpProxy Log Analysis (V15\Logging\HttpProxy\*\*.LOG)
stages.subtitle: Initial Access (T1190 - Exploit Public-Facing Application: Exchange HttpProxy SSRF)
stages.description: In the sunlit office building lobby, an unbadged visitor talks past the front-desk receptionist and persuades the desk clerk to print a temporary building pass. Specifically in Step 1, the intruder smuggles copied records out past the lobby badge turnstile in tiny disguised batches while everyday visitors and the front-desk receptionist go about their routine. stages.title: Stage 2: Exchange Management Log (MSExchange Management EventID 1) Set-OabVirtualDirectory & New-MailboxExportRequest
stages.subtitle: Persistence (T1505.003 - Server Software Component: Web Shell via Exchange Cmdlet)
stages.description: Instead of staying in the public waiting chairs, the visitor taps that pass at the lobby turnstile and walks down the hallway from one glass meeting room to the next. Here in Step 2 inside the office building, the intruder approaches the lobby badge turnstile disguised as a regular visitor without disturbing the public lobby waiting area. Using the proxied backend session, the actor invokes the Exchange Management cmdlet Set-OabVirtualDirectory (injecting JScript webshell code into the ExternalUrl property) followed by ResetOABVirtualDirectory (or New-MailboxExportRequest -FilePath "\\127.0.0.1\C$\inetpub\wwwroot\aspnet_client\supp.aspx") to write the configuration to disk. The Windows Event Log channel "MSExchange Management" records EventID 1 with every cmdlet parameter (logged in WinEvent Event 1 with LogChannel=MSExchange Management , EventID 1, ExecutedCmdlet=New-MailboxExportRequest / Set-OabVirtualDirectory, TargetFilePath=\\127.0.0.1\C$\inetpub\wwwroot\aspnet_client\supp.aspx so analysts can verify the exact actor and target artifact). stages.description: Inside the executive glass conference room, the intruder opens the unlocked cabinet and copies private project folders while staff walk by outside thinking they belong there. In this final step inside the office building, the intruder smuggles copied records out past the lobby badge turnstile in tiny disguised batches until the reception sign-in logbook catches the mismatch. Next, the follow-up artifact Sysmon EventID 1: ParentImage=C:\Windows\System32\inetsrv\w3wp.exe (-ap "MSExchangeOWAAppPool") -> Image=C:\Windows\System32\cmd.exe runs (which invokes or targets the host daemon/process , Sysmon EventID 1: ParentImage=C:\Windows\System32\inetsrv\w3wp.exe , -ap "MSExchangeOWAAppPool" -> Ima so that advances the scenario kill-chain under MITRE T1505.003 during "ASP.NET Dynamic Compilation , Temporary ASP.NET Files & w3wp.exe Child Shell , Sysmon EventID 1 & 11" , When the external actor requests POST /aspnet_client/supp while generating verifiable host or network telemetry for DFIR attribution). On the diagram, follow Step #3 / Link #3 (#3→ w3wp.exe -ap "MSExchangeOWAAppPool" spawning cmd.exe /c whoami / ⇠#3 ACK 1) from Node ③ (#3 Exchange Frontend HttpProxy) to Node ④ (#4 Exchange Backend EWS / ECP), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 OAB ExternalUrl & w3wp.exe).

steps.storyAnalogy: Inside the executive glass conference room, the intruder opens the unlocked cabinet and copies private project folders while staff walk by outside thinking they belong there.
